lines.li: [us] What's it like at court?
[them] Every word weighed, every bow measured, and every dinner a battle.
[us] It sounds exhausting.
[them] It is, and I wouldn't trade it for anything.
[us] Not even for a quiet life out here?
[them] Ask me again after a week of your quiet.
[them] Among my people, honor is earned in service and lost in a careless word.
[us,trait:Abrasive] Then I'd have lost mine by breakfast.
[us] Then I'll choose my words carefully.
[them] Wise, though I forgive a few careless ones from a friend.
[us] How should I address you, {OUTSIDER}?
[them] As {THEIRTITLE}, when others are listening.
[us] And when they aren't?
[them,likesyou] {OUTSIDER} will do, between friends.
[them] Still as {THEIRTITLE}, but with a little less bowing.
[them] I didn't expect to meet one of the Empire's titled this far from court.
[us] The Empire's reach is long.
[them,them:outranks] Long enough, {OURTITLE}, though you'll remember I stand above you.
[them,us:outranks] Long, and I see you stand above me, so I'll mind my manners.
[them,!them:outranks,!us:outranks] Long enough to find two of us equals in a field of mud.
[us] Out here, I'd rather we didn't stand on ceremony.
[them] Out here, I suppose we needn't.
[them] I'm told {NOBLE} holds the title of {NOBLETITLE} here.
[us] {NOBLE} does, though out here a title doesn't fetch the water.
[them] Then I should pay my respects before I leave.
[them] Your title carries favors, {OURTITLE}, the Empire answers those who serve it.
[us] So I've been told.
[them] Call on them wisely, the court remembers every one.
[us] Have you ever seen {LEADER}?
[them] Only from very far away, which is as close as anyone like me gets.
[us] And what is {LEADER} like, from far away?
[them] Very still, and very hard to forget.
[them] The Empire would have a place like this in order within a season.
[us] And would we still be free?
[them] Free to do things properly, yes.
[them] Our duel was fought properly, and I respect you for it.
[us] You fought well.
[them] As did you, and that is all that honor asks.
[us] Do you hope to rise higher, {OUTSIDER}?
[them] Everyone at court hopes, and the wise ones never say so aloud.
[us] And yet you just did.
[them] Then you see how far I trust you.
[us] Do you serve one of the titled?
[them] I serve the Empire, and the titled are how it tells me what to do.
[us] Is it a good life?
[them] It's an ordered one, which is most of what I wanted.
[them] At home the shuttles come and go like birds, and here it's all so quiet.
[us] Quiet suits us.
[them] I'm beginning to see why.
[them] Do you have any music here, or poetry?
[us,us:best:Artistic] Some, and I've been known to make a little of it myself.
[us] A little, mostly sung badly after supper.
[them] At court we would call that a beginning.
[them] The Empire doesn't lose wars, it only takes its time winning them.
[us] Do {WAR} know that?
[them,war:winning] They're learning.
[them] They will.
[us] The war with {WAR} isn't going your way, I hear.
[them] A town lost is a town the Empire means to take back.
[us] And the people in it?
[them] They are remembered, which is the most the Empire can promise anyone.
[them] Your gift was well chosen, and at court that is noticed.
[us] I'm glad it pleased you.
[them] It did, and I will say so to those who matter.
[them] You may bow, if your people do that sort of thing here.
[us] We don't, much, but you're welcome all the same.
[them,them:kind] Then welcome is enough.
[them] Then I'll take the welcome and forgive the rest.
[them] They say you hold one of the Empire's titles.
[us] I do, {OURTITLE}, for whatever it's worth out here.
[them,their:tribal] Our elders don't bow to sky people, but they'll be polite to you.
[them] It's worth a little, though not as much as a good harvest.
[them] Is it true {NOBLE} holds a title from the Empire?
[us] It is, {NOBLETITLE}, though we mostly just call them {NOBLE}.
[them,their:tribal] Then the sky people have one foot in your house.
[them] Good, as long as the Empire doesn't come calling for its taxes.
